stem: Which parent statement shows correct understanding of early hunger cues in a healthy full-term infant?

options.A: I will look for rooting, repeated hand-to-mouth movements, and lip smacking before the baby begins crying
options.B: I will wait for vigorous crying because crying is the earliest and most specific hunger cue
options.C: I should feed only at fixed clock times even when the baby shows clear hunger cues earlier
options.D: Any sucking behavior always means the baby is hungry and needs another feeding

rationale: AAP guidance supports responsive feeding for most healthy full-term infants. Typical hunger cues include rooting, hand-to-mouth behavior, lip licking/smacking, opening the mouth, increased alertness, and sucking behavior. Crying is a later hunger sign and can also have many non-hunger causes. Sucking is not uniquely specific for hunger because infants may also suck for comfort. Therefore A is the best answer.
educational_objective: Teach parents to respond to early infant hunger cues such as rooting, hand-to-mouth behavior, and lip smacking rather than waiting for crying or relying on rigid schedules.

correction_summary: Reframed the source recall question as parent-teaching validation, preserved the distinction between early cues and crying, and added the important limitation that sucking and crying are not uniquely specific for hunger.
audit_findings: A is directly supported. B incorrectly labels crying as early/specific; C conflicts with responsive feeding for healthy term infants; D overinterprets sucking. One best answer remains without schedule or intake-number precision. Independent adversarial second pass passed.
